source.title_on_document: LLM Randomness and Creativity: An Experiment on Human-AI Collaboration

supplement.where: The paper refers to no supplement, online appendix, preregistration, or data repository.
supplement.holds: Nothing referenced. Arm-level means and SDs of the creativity outcomes (semantic distance, RAT accuracy) are not printed anywhere, and the DAT regression is not reported.

paper_design_summary: Prolific participants were randomly assigned to one of nine cells of a 3 x 3 between-subjects design: no AI, an LLM chat assistant at temperature 0.1 (low randomness), or the same assistant at temperature 1.2 (high randomness), crossed with one of three tasks (Remote Associates Test, Alternate Uses Task, Divergent Association Task), each done for three rounds. AI was available but its use was not enforced. Performance was RAT accuracy and, for the AUT and DAT, the mean and maximum pairwise semantic distance (spaCy embeddings) among each participant's own responses.

studies.label: 3 x 3 online experiment: LLM randomness (none, temperature 0.1, temperature 1.2) x task (RAT, AUT, DAT)

participants.exclusions: 960 participants were recruited on Prolific (after a 40-person pilot). Those who did not complete the study or failed an attention check were excluded, leaving 775. The paper does not say how many of the 185 excluded had been assigned to a condition, so no count at assignment is given. Arm counts are from Table I and sum to 775 (AUT 213, DAT 245, RAT 317).
participants.who: Prolific participants, 48.4% female, mean age 41.89 (SD 12.40), paid $2.20
participants.quote: We then proceeded to recruit 960 participants (also from Prolific but different from those included in the pilot) and paid them $2.20 to complete the study. After excluding participants that did not complete the study or failed an attention check, we were left with 775 participants
participants.locator: PDF p. 3 (printed p. 1772), Section III.D Participants; arm Ns in Table I, PDF p. 4 (printed p. 1773)

ai_tool.name_model: Unnamed LLM; temperature 0.1 (low randomness) or 1.2 (high randomness). The paper does not name the model or provider.
ai_tool.how_used: A chat panel ("Ask AI") beside the task on a custom platform; participants could query the assistant for suggestions but use was not enforced. Only 251 of 519 participants with AI available used it (AUT 87 of 145, RAT 94 of 212, DAT 70 of 162 by subtraction from the non-use counts printed).

task.description: Each participant did one task for three rounds: RAT (find a fourth word linking three cue words; convergent), AUT (creative uses for a common object, e.g. paperclip; at least 3 ideas per round per Figure 1), or DAT (list ten words as unrelated as possible).
task.duration: not stated (three rounds; time on task used as a regression control)

outcomes.name: AUT average semantic distance among a participant's own responses
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: spaCy en_core_web_md 300-dimensional embeddings of each response; mean of all pairwise cosine distances (1 - similarity) within a participant's set of responses. Paper calls it creative performance / semantic diversity. Coded flexibility because it measures variety among one person's own ideas, not across people. OLS on condition dummies (reference = low randomness) controlling for duration_seconds and AI_used.

contrasts.reported: Avg Semantic Distance: NoAI -0.002 (0.044), not significant; intercept 0.623 (0.040)***; regression controls duration_seconds -0.000 (0.000)*** and AI_used 0.040 (0.039). Sign reversed: coefficient is NoAI relative to Low randomness. Regression N not printed.
Avg Semantic Distance: HighRandomness -0.008 (0.037), not significant.

contrasts.treatment_arm: AUT_High, participants who used the AI only
contrasts.control_arm: AUT_Low, participants who used the AI only
contrasts.reported: "average semantic distance in the High-Randomness condition was 0.51 versus 0.31 in the Low-Randomness condition. While this difference is only marginally significant"; no SE, n, or exact p printed. Subsample selected on post-assignment AI use.

outcomes.question: with_ai

Max Semantic Distance: HighRandomness -0.012 (0.045), not significant. Among AI users only, the paper says "consistent results are found for maximum semantic distance" with no numbers.

outcomes.measure_detail: Number of correct responses divided by the number of problems attempted. OLS on condition dummies (reference = low randomness) controlling for duration_seconds and AI_used.

"LLMs (irrespective of their level of randomness in the 0.1-1.2 range) increase accuracy (on average, from 45 to 55%, p < .05)"; among those who used the AI, "accuracy was 64%, p < .001". No SE or test printed.

eligibility.reason: Individuals on Prolific were randomly assigned to no AI or an LLM assistant (two temperatures) on creativity tasks (PDF p. 2). 775 people analyzed; each task subsample also exceeds 50 (AUT 213, DAT 245, RAT 317; Table I). Outcomes are computed on participants' responses (semantic distance for AUT/DAT, accuracy for RAT). Caveats: AI use was optional (251 of 519 used it), the main regressions control for post-assignment AI use, the RAT outcome is convergent (codebook open question), and the AUT/DAT measures are within-person variety rather than rated creativity.

one_line_finding: Neither AI availability nor LLM temperature changed AUT semantic distance (NoAI -0.002, SE 0.044; HighRandomness -0.008, SE 0.037; Table II, p. 4) or DAT scores (not reported), while AI availability raised RAT accuracy from 45 to 55 percent (p < .05; Discussion, p. 3) though the Table III NoAI coefficient controlling for AI use is -0.044 (SE 0.055).
open_questions: Do the 775 analyzed include everyone assigned who completed? The paper does not say whether attention-check failures occurred before or after assignment, so no count at assignment is available.

The Table II/III regressions control for AI_used, a post-assignment variable, so the NoAI coefficient is not the intention-to-treat effect of AI availability. Unadjusted arm means and SDs of the performance outcomes are not printed (Table I has only survey constructs).
Whether AUT/DAT within-person semantic distance should be coded flexibility (variety among one person's own ideas) or overall creativity (the paper's 'creative performance'; DAT's standard score).
The standard-error type for the OLS regressions is not stated.
notes: The task is named 'Remote Associates Test' in the abstract and 'Random Associates Task (RAT)' in Section III.A. The paper also reports, for AUT, a correlation between the share of AI-generated words incorporated and semantic distance (r = -.399, p < .001; PDF p. 3), which is correlational within AI users and not a contrast between arms. Self-reported outcomes (process and outcome satisfaction, ownership, intrinsic motivation, perceived effort) were also analyzed and are not listed because they are not scored on the output. Outcome satisfaction was lower in No-AI than Low (p < .01) and High (p < .001) for the RAT, Holm-adjusted (PDF p. 3). AI non-use counts: AUT 58 of 145, RAT 118 of 212, DAT 92 of 162; chi2(2, 519) = 10.96, p = .004 (PDF p. 3).
